subject: Vendor EIN evidence: portal screenshot + W-9 (next steps for PO)
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina@evergran.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@evergran.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evergran W-9 + portal screenshot for EIN verification

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the onboarding checklist — attaching the signed W-9 and a screenshot from our payroll portal showing the EIN and timestamp. We captured the portal page and a short OTP log excerpt from the admin audit to show the timestamped access.

Attachments: Evergran_W9_20260608.pdf (signed W-9), ein_portal_screenshot_20260608.png (portal landing page w/ EIN and timestamp), otp_log_evergran_0608.txt (audit snippet)

Let me know if you need the IRS 147C or a bank letter; we can pull the 147C but it takes ~3–5 business days. We’re aiming to have the PO issued this week so we can start onboarding the integration team.

Best,
Lina Torres
Head of Finance Operations
Evergran Systems
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina@evergran.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evergran W-9 + portal screenshot for EIN verification

Hi Lina — thanks for the quick turnaround and for including the portal screenshot. A couple of quick items from procurement / tax side: 

- We need confirmation that the EIN in the screenshot exactly matches the W-9 (number + entity name). I can do a parity check but need the W-9 to be a PDF with an embedded signature (looks ok from the preview).
- Please confirm the portal screenshot shows the admin account used and that the timestamp is server-side (not local file metadata). The audit OTP log helps — can you add a one-line statement in the body confirming that the OTP log is generated by Evergran's auth service and not manually edited?
- If the IRS 147C is available, that will speed things up if there is any mismatch.

Next steps on our side: Ben will run the EIN through our automated TIN match process and Karthik will advise if we need a bank letter or tele-notary alternative. Assuming clean match, procurement will issue a provisional PO that will convert to a full PO after payment terms are reconciled.

Naomi
Vendor Onboarding Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Lina Torres <lina@evergran.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evergran W-9 + portal screenshot for EIN verification

Quick note from tax verification: I ran the EIN through our matcher against IRS TIN data (internal tool). The numeric sequence formatted on the W-9 preview matches the portal screenshot at a glance but the entity name on the W-9 is slightly abbreviated vs. our canonical vendor name (Evergran Systems, Inc. vs Evergran Systems).

Karthik — do you want to request the 147C now or should we ask for a bank letter first? If the 147C turnaround is multiple business days and procurement needs to move, we can accept a notarized bank letter + signed attestation as provisional evidence and proceed with a conditional PO. Lina — would Evergran be able to provide a bank letter signed by your bank (scanned PDF) if that’s faster?

If we get provisional evidence today, I can request procurement create PR-4821 as a provisional PO and flag it for conversion once legal/tax confirms final evidence.

—Ben
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina@evergran.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evergran W-9 + portal screenshot for EIN verification

Thanks all — Lina, a bank letter (on bank letterhead, showing the legal entity and EIN) will be sufficient for us to clear procurement conditional PO. If you can include a one-line attestation in the email body that the portal screenshot and OTP log are server-generated (as Naomi requested) that will resolve the minor name formatting mismatch.

We will:
- Issue a provisional PO with net-45 terms (Procure link: https://procure.redwood.internal/requests/PR-4821)
- Mark invoice approval pending once PR-4821 converts to full PO after final evidence

Lina — can you confirm ETA on the bank letter? If it’s >3 business days we’ll still issue a provisional PO but leave payment on hold.

Karthik Iyer
Tax & Compliance, Redwood Inference
